theorem.bezout_bound: Two plane conics without a common component have intersection length at most four over the algebraic closure, hence at most four compatible projective Q-classes.
theorem.conic_pair_cut: For direction nodes y,y', the equality of the two displayed ratios is N_y(R)D_y'(R)-N_y'(R)D_y(R)=0.  On the residual Q-plane this is a conic.  If two such conics have no common component, every compatible finite root lies in their zero-dimensional intersection.
theorem.finite_slope_bound: For each compatible Q-class, the direction equations are inconsistent, slope-free/contained, or determine one scalar z.  Thus the no-common-component branch has at most four finite noncontained parameters.
theorem.low_degree_transfer: At A=385 every finite root in a separated rank-6 boundary bucket is represented by a projective Q-class with deg Q<5.
theorem.projective_safety: The endpoint-uniform theorem contributes at most the single projective endpoint, so the branch total is at most 5<=6.
theorem.residual: If every useful conic pair has a common component on the fixed two-core Q-plane, that common-component branch remains as the named fixed-two-core residual.
theorem.two_point_reduction: A fixed two-point base core imposes two independent conditions on polynomials deg Q<5, leaving a three-dimensional vector space Q=E R with deg R<3, i.e. a projective plane.
